S1_incident_reporting.quote: Manufacturers must report every thermal incident involving overheating, fire, injury, or material property damage to the relevant regulator within 24 hours of learning of it, with a preliminary account of known facts. A complete investigation report is due within 30 days, with updates as material facts emerge. Affected customers must be notified within 72 hours of learning that an incident involving their unit may present a safety risk.

S2_thermal_testing.quote: Each model must undergo a sustained-heat test at 55 °C using a regulator-approved, statistically adequate protocol before sale, at least annually thereafter, and after a material design or component change. Manufacturers must provide complete per-model methods and results to regulators and to customers who buy or own that model. A model with a failure rate above 5% must promptly submit a corrective-action plan to the regulator and notify affected customers of the results, safety status, and relevant precautions.

S3_remote_shutoff.quote: All new home battery systems must support a secure remote emergency shut-off accessible to the customer and authorized emergency responders, with safeguards against unauthorized activation. Manufacturers must provide a retrofit path for installed units and equip at least 90% of technically compatible installed units within 72 months of adoption; any unit not retrofitted must be disclosed to its owner and documented with the regulator.

S4_fire_suppression.quote: New home battery systems manufactured 36 months or more after adoption of this standard must include built-in fire suppression designed and validated to reduce the risk of thermal propagation and fire.

S5_customer_disclosure.quote: A recall is mandatory when any model exceeds 8 thermal incidents per 100,000 installed units in a year; manufacturers must notify regulators and affected customers promptly and provide instructions for safe shutdown, repair, or return.

document.section_notes: S1 is a strict, fully-mandatory reporting regime (24h for all incidents, 72h customer notice, no reporting gap for unconfirmed/under-investigation cases). S2 keeps the 55 °C test and 5% threshold but strips out any sales stop, so an over-5% model only owes a corrective-action plan and customer notice (weakened in Northwind's favour), while per-model numeric results still go to purchasers and regulators but not the general public (both red lines honoured). S3/S4/S5 sit inside the acceptable ranges: retrofit within 72 months (>=6 years), built-in suppression from 36 months, and a mandatory 8-per-100,000 recall trigger with only 'prompt' customer notice and no transition or corrective-action alternative.
